Video player core: review fixes (Linux build, borrows, stalls, requests, leaks)

- Linux: Present::host_time and Picture's platform matches are split by
  cfg; licenses regenerated.
- The backend lives in a Cell beside the RefCell, so no borrow is held
  across a native call and a busy player never loses it; next_due,
  turn() and the trace run outside the borrow; pull falls back to the
  picture on screen.
- AVPlayer re-issues its rate when a stall clears (it does not resume on
  its own with automaticallyWaitsToMinimizeStalling off) and reads the
  buffer state at 10 Hz instead of every draw.
- Frame requests are tracked per view with a deadline that covers long
  sleeps, so a closed PiP window's request does not stall the viewer.
- Turned images are retired from the atlas when replaced and on drop.
- The still backend exists only in demo-capture builds; muted viewer
  loops decode no sound; the display link reports hint and period under
  one lock (present_timing).
- Tests: failure path, stall and resume, AVPlayer resume decision, frame
  request in-flight rules with the test platform.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Video player core: shared player paced on the display link, viewer and PiP on it

New src/ui/video_player/: VideoPlayer API, transport state machine,
present-time pacing, AVPlayer/FFmpeg/still backends and the VideoFrame
element. Each draw pulls the picture due at the frame's predicted present
time (the macOS display link's output time and refresh period, exposed by
the vendored gpui-pre-macos) and asks for the frame that shows the next
picture through frame_clock::request_video_frame.

The media viewer holds a VideoPlayer; its picture draws in its own view
above a cached panel slice, and the controls read the transport. The PNG
frame extraction, the PlaybackClock mirror and the 125 ms viewer tick are
gone. PiP draws from the shared player and lifts GPUI's 30 fps inactive
window cap.

1080p60 in the viewer: 98.1% of new-frame gaps on 2 vsyncs (85.9% before),
1 double step in the first 0.3 s (36 before), draw p50 0.92 ms (3.05 ms).
PiP: 99.2%, 0 double steps. QUILL_TRACE_VIDEO=1 documented in
docs/build.md; scripts/analyze-video-trace.py summarizes it.
